payload.report: The patient has profound HIV immunosuppression (CD4 3 cells/mm³) and diffuse pustular lesions progressing from genitourinary symptoms, indicating a disseminated infectious process. Skin biopsy showing viral inclusions and positive DNA PCR with F13L gene mutations confirm orthopoxvirus (mpox) infection. Negative HSV, VZV, and fungal tests exclude common mimics, and repeated positive skin PCR further supports mpox. Noninfectious pustular disease and classic disseminated STIs are ruled out. However, blood/CSF mpox PCR and visceral imaging were not obtained, so direct hematogenous or organ dissemination remains unconfirmed. Therefore, the leading diagnosis is disseminated mpox infection with high but not absolute confidence.
